valley.drawingAlt: A snail on a small hill in the fog. Far off, a bright meadow stands above the clouds.
locals: Always climb. Never go down. Down is where the fog lives.
This hill is the highest place there is. I checked, all the way around.
Brume stopped climbing long ago. Brume calls it resting.

notes.title: Stuck on a small hill
notes.science: A climber that only ever goes up stops on the first top it finds, even when a taller one stands close by.
notes.limits: Real searchers can remember, jump, or look far.
notes.counter: Sometimes the small hill is good enough, and the climb down costs too much.
notes.question: When did you go down to get further up?

sources.label: Optimization by Simulated Annealing, Kirkpatrick, Gelatt and Vecchi, 1983

notes.title: Explore or stay
notes.science: Every searcher chooses between using what it knows and trying something new. Too little trying keeps you on the small hill.
notes.limits: A map of land is not a map of every choice.
notes.counter: A guide who sees one ridge further can help more than a jump in the dark.
notes.question: Who saw further than you?

sources.label: Exploration and Exploitation in Organizational Learning, March, 1991
